about: Benchmark for the one-sentence similarity filter. Each filter is only a sentence; the passages are test content, never used to build the filter. direct = on topic and names it; indirect = on topic without the obvious word (tests the concept, not the keyword); hardNeg = has the word or a near topic but is off topic; mixed = ordinary text that turns on topic part-way (streaming: must not fire before, should fire soon after). Every passage of one filter is also an off-topic test for the other filters.
baselineText: The office moved to the third floor last spring, and most people say the light is better up there. Meetings now happen in the long room by the windows, and the printer sits by the door, which causes a small queue every morning. The council has promised to repair the pavement outside before winter, though nobody has seen any workers yet. On Tuesdays the market sets up in the square with stalls selling books, plants, old records and second-hand tools. My neighbour is learning Spanish from an app and practises by talking to her houseplants. The bus timetable changed again in September, so the last service now leaves the station at half past eleven. Last weekend we walked along the canal, watched the boats go through the locks and talked about where to go on holiday next year. The new receptionist starts on Monday, so someone needs to show her where everything is and set up her email account. The library has started opening late on Thursdays, which is handy for anyone who works during the day. Our street is having its annual tidy-up next month, and the residents' group is asking for volunteers to bring brooms and bin bags. My cousin finally passed his driving test on the third attempt and has already planned a trip to see his friends up north. The internet at home keeps dropping in the evenings, and the provider says an engineer can come round on the fourteenth. I have been meaning to sort the cupboard under the stairs for months, but there is always something more urgent to do.
